To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

state-resolved quantum dynamical calculations are performed for the Ne + D2 (+) → NeD(+) + D reaction, and the results show that vibrational excitation of D2 (+) is more efficient in enhancing reaction cross sections than the translational and rotational excitations.
vibrational excitation of reactant is much efficient than translational and rotation excitations in enhancing reaction cross sections.

the proton transfer reaction is much more efficient when the reactant is in a higher vibrational state, the differential cross sections are forward-backward peaked at lower collision energy and become forward biased at higher collision energy, and the forward bias can be explained by the larger J partial wave contribution to the differential cross sections.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the state-resolved dynamics for the Ne + D2 (+) ( v = 0-1, j = 1) → NeD(+) + D reaction.
the dynamics of proton transfer reaction NeH(+) formation from the ground state Ne + H2 (v = 2, j =0) collision.
the state-resolved integral and differential cross sections for the title reaction, which is important for the understanding of the reaction mechanism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LZHH potential energy surfaces are able to reproduce all the experimental data and theoretical results for this reaction.
vibrational excitation of reactant H2(+) is the dominant dynamical factor for the Ne + HD(+) reaction.
vibrational excitation of reactant is the most important factor to enhance the reactivity of the title reaction, which is consistent with the previous theoretical studies on the Ne + HCl reaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the state-to-state quantum dynamics calculations on the accurate LZHH potential surface can reproduce the integral cross sections and the differential cross sections for the proton transfer process Ne + H2(+)(v = 0, j = 1) → NeH(+)(v′, j′) + H, which are important in the interpretation of the available experiments.
the proton transfer reaction is a complex-forming process, and vibrational excitation is the dominant factor in enhancing the reaction probability.

the LZHH PES is able to reproduce the experimental cross sections for the title reaction.
